pr_title: Add commands to navigate frames with same tag
pr_comments:
I'm not sure about this solution. Should we add new commands or a user-defined configuration flag to modify `GotoPreviousFrame`/`GotoNextFrame` behavior?
I just found that we can pass parameters to commands :P 
Solution which uses user-defined flag should be better than current one, since lots of duplicated code exist now.
> I just found that we can pass parameters to commands :P 

:smile: Anyway in this case I'm not talking about command parameters.

I'm talking about a preference option in [pref.xml](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/master/data/pref.xml#L68) that you can check using [Preference::instance()](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/master/src/app/pref/preferences.h#L45) and that can be changed from [OptionsWindow](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/master/src/app/commands/cmd_options.cpp#L39) ([options.xml](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/master/data/widgets/options.xml))

The [UndoCommand](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/master/src/app/commands/cmd_undo.cpp#L71) is a good example about one command which its behavior changes with a user-defined option.
I'm not a professional digital artist but I think during working I'll need both `goto next frame` and `goto next frame with same tag` as well and might use them frequently. As my opinion, these two commands should be available at the same time. Defined their behaviour with global preference looks not very reasonable to me.

What do you think?
> I think during working I'll need both goto next frame and goto next frame with same tag

You are right. Also it was my original idea in #556 :smile: I'll merge this PR, it looks fine as it is (don't worry about command params).

Thanks for your help! :wink: 
Wait! The tag bug is still there!
I'll fix it. Don't worry.

issue_context.title: Make , and . keys move in the loop section
issue_context.body: If a loop is configured, we should be able to use , and . keys to move through the loop (and left/right arrows to move outside the loop)

review_comments: I didn't check this in runtime, but I think `tag` can be nullptr, so this line crashes if the command is used in animations without tags.
